title: Demography and Population Statistics
curriculum_locator: Stat H-203 Demography & Stat H-210 Lab; University of Dhaka four-year B.S. Honours Statistics curriculum, starting session 2023–2024

units.title: Sources, Evaluation & Quality of Demographic Data
scope: Primary demographic data systems: population censuses (de jure vs de facto), vital registration, and demographic surveys
Types of demographic errors: coverage errors and content errors (post-enumeration surveys, dual-system estimation)
Evaluation of age reporting errors and digit preference: Whipple's Index, Myers' Blended Index, and Bachi's Index
United Nations Age-Sex Accuracy Index and age heaping diagnosis
Smoothing techniques for age data: moving average filters and Carrier-Farrag graduation formulas

units.title: Population Composition, Sex Ratios & Age Structural Dynamics
scope: Age-sex structures and population pyramid typologies: expansive, stationary, and constrictive profiles
Sex ratios at birth, sex ratios by age, and masculinity proportion indicators
Demographic dependency ratios: child, old-age, and total dependency ratios
The Demographic Transition Model (five stages) and demographic dividend dynamics
Population aging metrics: median age, aging index, and Bongaarts aging decomposition

units.title: Measures of Mortality & Standardization Techniques
scope: Crude Death Rate (CDR), age-specific death rates (ASDR), and force of mortality mu(x)
Infant mortality rate (IMR): neonatal, early neonatal, post-neonatal, and child mortality rates
Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) and causes of death cause-deleted mortality analysis
Confounding role of age composition and rationale for rate standardization
Direct standardization using reference populations and Indirect standardization (Standardized Mortality Ratio / SMR)

units.title: Life Tables: Mathematical Construction, Complete & Abridged Models
scope: Fundamental life table functions: q(x), l(x), d(x), L(x), T(x), and expectation of life e(x)
Mathematical relationships between central death rates m(x) and mortality probabilities q(x)
Average fraction of last year of life a(x) and Chiang, Greville, and Reed-Merrell formulas
Abridged life tables vs complete life tables and graduation techniques
Applications of life tables in actuarial science, public health, and survival analysis

units.title: Measures of Fertility, Nuptiality & Reproduction
scope: Crude Birth Rate (CBR), General Fertility Rate (GFR), and General Marital Fertility Rate (GMFR)
Age-Specific Fertility Rates (ASFR) and Total Fertility Rate (TFR)
Gross Reproduction Rate (GRR) and Net Reproduction Rate (NRR) incorporating female survival schedules
Replacement-level fertility (NRR = 1) and sub-replacement demographic implications
Nuptiality analysis: singulate mean age at marriage (SMAM) and Bongaarts' proximate determinants of fertility

units.title: Mathematical Models of Population Growth
scope: Linear and arithmetic growth models: constant increments and limitations
Geometric compounding growth model and compound interest analogies
Continuous exponential growth model P(t) = P(0) e^(rt) and doubling time formulations
Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth model: differential formulation, carrying capacity K, and inflection points
Curve fitting of logistic models: Rhodes method, three-point method, and non-linear least squares

units.title: Stable and Stationary Population Theory (Lotka System)
scope: Stationary population model as a special case of life table person-years (r = 0, NRR = 1)
Lotka's continuous stable population model: age distribution c(x) = b e^(-rx) l(x)
Derivation of the fundamental characteristic equation for the intrinsic rate of natural increase r
Numerical solution of the characteristic equation via Euler-Lotka polynomials
Intrinsic birth rate b, intrinsic death rate d, mean length of generation, and Coale-Lopez weak ergodicity

units.title: Migration Analysis, Intercensal Estimation & Cohort-Component Projections
scope: Demographic balancing equation: natural increase and net migration components
Internal and international migration metrics: in-migration, out-migration, net and gross migration rates
Intercensal population estimation: arithmetic, geometric, and vital statistics balancing methods
Census survival ratio methods: forward and reverse survival estimation of intercensal migration
Cohort-component population projection methodology: matrix formulation and projection pipelines
